overall: At 1:00 AM ET, Atlanta is sitting at 73.4°F with a running max of 75.2°F and a dewpoint of 71.6°F — an extremely muggy overnight that suggests a deeply moist airmass in place. Temperatures are gently cooling at -1.8°F/hr, consistent with typical overnight radiational cooling, but the near-saturated conditions (dewpoint within 2°F of air temp) indicate the atmosphere is loaded with moisture heading into the heating hours.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful spread: GFS and HRRR are in lockstep at 79.0°F while NBM (82.1°F) and ECMWF (83.0°F) run 3–4°F warmer, suggesting the global and mesoscale guidance is capturing different convective or mixing scenarios for the afternoon. The ensemble signals both center in the 80–82°F range, lending support to the higher end of the GFS/HRRR solution rather than the lower.
max_temp_prediction: With GFS and HRRR anchoring at 79°F but the full-model average near 80.8°F and the Tier 1 odd-model ensemble pointing firmly to 81–82°F, the balance of evidence favors a daily high in the low-to-mid 80s. The very high overnight dewpoint will keep the overnight low elevated and supports robust afternoon mixing, nudging the forecast above the GFS/HRRR floor. Confidence is moderate — the 4°F model spread and mixed ensemble tier signals (Tier 1 vs. Tier 4) introduce meaningful uncertainty, but the preponderance of guidance clusters near 81°F.
